sections.h2: Where is Weymouth, MA, and what are its four villages?
sections.html:
Weymouth is a Norfolk County city on the South Shore, bordered by Hingham Bay and Boston Harbor to the north. It covers 21.58 square miles, but 4.81 of that is water, and the 2020 Census counted 57,437 residents.

Residents describe four districts. North Weymouth sits north of the Church, North and Green Street junction and has the waterfront parks and beaches. South Weymouth lies mostly south of Route 3 and holds Weymouth High School and South Shore Hospital. East Weymouth has Whitman's Pond, Jackson Square and Town Hall, plus many Victorian houses. Weymouth Landing spans about a mile around Weston Park at the Braintree line.

Quincy, Braintree and Holbrook lie to the west, Abington and Rockland to the south, and Hingham to the east. Grape Island, Slate Island and Sheep Island in the Boston Harbor Islands National Recreation Area also belong to Weymouth.

Weymouth began in 1622 as the Wessagusset colony, which makes it the second-oldest settlement in Massachusetts after Plymouth. The first attempt failed, but settlers who stayed formed the base of the permanent town, which took the Weymouth name in 1635.

Shoemaking was the main industry from the early 1700s until Stetson Shoe closed in 1973. The old Naval Air Station South Weymouth closed in the 1990s, and the land is being redeveloped as Union Point. Weymouth also voted in 1999 to replace town meeting with a mayor and council, ending 365 years of continuous town meeting. The first mayor took office in 2000.

sections.h2: How do Weymouth's waterfront and climate affect homes?
sections.html:
Water shapes much of Weymouth, from Hingham Bay to the Back River and Fore River. Wikipedia notes the city is especially vulnerable to sea level rise. It also describes North Weymouth waterfront cottages being bought and rebuilt, so condition and flood exposure vary a great deal from street to street.

Average precipitation runs about 44 inches a year, with January highs near 39 degrees. If you own near the shore:

  • Pull your flood insurance policy and any elevation certificate.
  • Document sea wall, bulkhead or drainage repairs with dates.
  • Tell buyers or the cash buyer about past water in the basement.

Put the history in writing for any buyer, since hiding it tends to surface at inspection.

sections.h2: What is the East Weymouth housing like, and what do older houses need?
sections.html:
East Weymouth has many Queen Anne, shingle and colonial revival houses, with restoration under way on streets such as Hillcrest Road. Whatever the village, it is worth having the roof, heating system, wiring and porches looked at before you decide how to sell.

The city's 2010 housing count showed 64 percent owner-occupied and 35 percent renter-occupied, so renters live in a large share of the housing. If you inherited one of these houses and live elsewhere, a repair list can be the biggest hurdle to a traditional listing.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads serve Weymouth?
sections.html:
Weymouth High School in South Weymouth is the city's only public high school and enrolls more than 1,800 students. The Maria Weston Chapman Middle School opened in September 2022, and eight primary schools and an early childhood center complete the system. Private options include South Shore Christian Academy and the Catholic Sacred Heart and St. Francis Xavier schools.

Routes 3, 3A, 18, 53, 58 and 139 pass through the city. The MBTA Greenbush Line stops at East Weymouth and Weymouth Landing/East Braintree, and the Kingston Line stops at South Weymouth. If your house is within reach of a station, say so in any listing.

sections.h2: What is Union Point, and what else is around Weymouth?
sections.html:
Union Point is the redevelopment of the former Naval Air Station South Weymouth. Wikipedia describes plans for a parkway, residences, a sports facility and a movie studio, and notes the site has hosted several film shoots. The 25-acre Union Point Sports Complex is already open.

Wikipedia reports 700 acres of parks and conservation land across 46 sites. North Weymouth has Great Esker Park, George Lane Beach and Webb Memorial State Park, and in spring hundreds of thousands of alewife herring run up the brook between the Back River and Whitman's Pond. Abigail Adams was born in Weymouth, and her birthplace is a local landmark.

sections.h2: How do Massachusetts property tax abatements work for Weymouth owners?
sections.html:
Weymouth assessors follow the state process explained by the Appellate Tax Board. You can seek an abatement if the assessed value is above the fair cash value as of the January 1 valuation date, or if an exemption or classification applies.

  • Bills in quarterly cities are generally due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1.
  • The abatement application is due by the first installment date, generally February 1 in those cities.
  • Assessors have three months, and no answer counts as a denial.
  • You then have three months to appeal to the Appellate Tax Board.

Weymouth's assessing office publishes its own schedule. Ask it which billing pattern applies and where to get the abatement form.

sections.h2: What does a Weymouth seller pay to record the deed?
sections.html:
Weymouth deeds are recorded with the Norfolk County Registry of Deeds. The registry charges $156 to record a deed and an excise tax of $2.28 for each $500 of the stated price. Its own example shows a $155,000 deed owing $706.80, and the excise must be paid with an attorney's check or bank check.

On a $600,000 sale the same rate gives $2,736. A municipal lien certificate costs $81 at the registry, and a mortgage discharge is $106 per marginal reference, so budget for these small items too.

sections.h2: Cash sale versus listing for a Weymouth house
sections.html:
A Weymouth listing can draw plenty of attention, particularly near the commuter rail, but showings and repairs take time. A cash sale suits owners who want to close on their own schedule, who inherited a house, or who face a repair bill they do not want to carry.

Ask any buyer for proof of funds, a written contract and a clear statement of who pays each closing cost. Then compare the net you would keep from each option.

faqs.q: Is Weymouth, MA a city or a town?
faqs.a: Weymouth has a city form of government but keeps "Town of Weymouth" as its official name. Voters replaced town meeting with a mayor and council in 1999.

faqs.q: How many train stations are in Weymouth?
faqs.a: Three. The Greenbush Line stops at East Weymouth and Weymouth Landing/East Braintree, and the Kingston Line stops at South Weymouth.

faqs.q: How much is the deed excise tax in Norfolk County?
faqs.a: The Norfolk County Registry of Deeds charges $2.28 for each $500 of the stated price or fraction of $500, payable by attorney's check or bank check at recording.

faqs.q: Which parts of Weymouth are near the water?
faqs.a: North Weymouth faces Hingham Bay and Boston Harbor. The Back River and Fore River also run through the city, so check flood exposure street by street.

faqs.q: What happened to the Naval Air Station in South Weymouth?
faqs.a: It closed in the 1990s under the Base Realignment and Closure process, and the land is being redeveloped as Union Point, a mixed-use community with homes, a sports complex and film production space.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Weymouth house as is?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell as is to an investor or cash buyer. Disclose known problems in writing, and expect the offer to reflect the repairs the house needs.
